title: PGA Tour Champions golfer Matt Gogel suspended six months for betting on PGA Tour events
text:
Matt Gogel claimed he unknowingly placed small recreational golf betting wagers in 2024, resulting in a six-month PGA Tour Champions suspension.

Matt Gogel plays his shot from the fifth tee during the final round of the Boeing Classic 2026 at The Club at Snoqualmie Ridge on Aug. 16, 2026, in Snoqualmie, Wash.
"I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf. I made an honest mistake, and I look forward to playing in 2027 on the PGA Tour Champions.
"The PGA Tour claimed that Gogel never once bet in a tournament he participated in. However, he violated the Tour’s integrity program where wagering on PGA-sanctioned events is prohibited. Matt Gogel of the United States hits a tee shot from the 1st during the second round of the Rogers Charity Classic 2026 at Canyon Meadows Golf & CC on Aug. 22, 2026, in Calgary, Alberta, Canada..
In 2023, Vince India and Jake Staiano on the Korn Ferry Tour were suspended six months and three months, respectively, for similarly placing bets on PGA Tour competitions. Gogel, 55, had just one PGA Tour victory in his career, which came at the Pebble Beach Pro-Am in 2002.
However, after his first career on Tour, he became a golf broadcaster with The Golf Channel and CBS Sports. When he turned 50, Gogel joined the PGA Tour Champions, which is the senior circuit of the golf organization.
